description:
What If You Got Close to the Monster at the Center of Our Galaxy?

Episode 72 of a daily journey through the universe. 🕳️
Sagittarius A*: the supermassive black hole at the center of the Milky Way, about 4 million times the Sun's mass and 26,000 light-years away. How stars racing around it proved it exists (Nobel Prize 2020), and its first image in 2022.

➡️ Tomorrow, Episode 73: Next stop, quasars. The brightest objects in the universe.
Start from Episode 1 "Leaving Earth" on the channel.
Follow so you don't miss a stop. A new episode every day.

Images: NASA (public domain)
Narration: AI voice

#space #sagittariusa #astronomy #shorts #science

segments.text: There's a monster at the center of our galaxy, four million times heavier than the Sun.
At the center of our Milky Way, about twenty-six thousand light-years away, hides a monster.
segments.headline: The heart of the Milky Way

segments.text: A black hole about four million times heavier than the Sun.
We can't see the center with normal light. Thick clouds of dust block it. But infrared light passes through.
segments.headline: Hidden by dust

segments.text: For decades, two teams, one led by Reinhard Genzel and one by Andrea Ghez, tracked stars orbiting something invisible.
segments.headline: Watching stars race

segments.text: One star, called S two, circles it every sixteen years, reaching thousands of kilometers per second.
Only a black hole could be that heavy and that small. Their work won the Nobel Prize in Physics in twenty twenty.
segments.headline: Nobel Prize, 2020

segments.text: In twenty twenty-two, the Event Horizon Telescope revealed its first image: a glowing ring of hot gas around a dark shadow.
segments.headline: The first image, 2022

segments.text: Compared to other giant black holes, ours is quiet. It only nibbles on gas. But some black holes are anything but quiet.
segments.headline: A quiet giant

segments.text: Tomorrow, black holes so hungry they outshine whole galaxies. Next stop: quasars. Which part surprised you most? Tell me in the comments, and follow for tomorrow's stop.
